'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbas]], [[Russia–Ukraine relations]]
**[[Kremlin Press Secretary|Kremlin Spokesman]] [[Dmitry Peskov]] warns that the delivery and [[Ukraine]]'s first operational [[Military deployment|deployment]] of the [[Turkey|Turkish]] [[Bayraktar TB2]] in [[Donbas]] may "destabilize the situation" in the region. Ukraine carried out its first strikes against [[separatist]] forces using the Bayraktar [[unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drone]] yesterday. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/kremlin-says-turkish-drones-risk-destabilising-situation-east-ukraine-2021-10-27/ (Reuters)]
**[[Ukrainian Ground Forces|Ukrainian troops]] regain control of the village of Staromaryivka in the so-called "grey zone" between Ukraine and the [[Donetsk People's Republic]] (DPR), according to DPR Foreign Minister Natalya Nikonorova. [https://tass.com/world/1354741 (TASS)]
*[[Islamic State insurgency in Iraq (2017–present)|Islamic State insurgency in Iraq]]
**Eleven people are killed and 26 more injured as angry villagers attack residents of Nahr Al-Imam in retaliation for yesterday's [[Islamic State]] attack in the nearby village of Al-Rashad, [[Diyala Governorate]], which killed 15 people. The victims were not however connected to the attack. [https://english.alaraby.co.uk/news/iraqis-kill-11-blaming-neighbouring-village-attack (The New Arab)]
*[[October 2021 Tehreek-e-Labbaik Pakistan protests]]
**Four policemen are killed and 263 more are injured during clashes with supporters of the banned [[Far-right politics|far-right]] [[Islamic extremism|Islamic extremist]]  [[Tehreek-e-Labbaik Pakistan]] party in [[Lahore]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/27/pakistani-police-killed-at-tlp-protest (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Papua conflict]]
**A report by the [[United Nations]] and the [[government of Papua New Guinea]] finds that thousands of Papuans from [[Indonesia]] have crossed into the remote border areas of western [[Papua New Guinea]]. In one of the areas, the sole police commander, Terry Dap, has asked the central government in [[Port Moresby]] to help reduce the influx of [[asylum seeker]]s into Papua New Guinea. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/454356/west-papuans-flee-from-conflict-into-remote-png-area (RNZ)]
*[[October 2021 Sudanese coup d'état]]
**The [[African Union]] suspends [[Sudan]] in response to Monday's [[Sudanese Armed Forces|military]] [[coup d'état|coup]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/african-union-suspends-sudan-after-military-coup/a-59638408 (DW)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Pope Francis]] blesses two large bells headed to [[Ukraine]] and [[Ecuador]]. The bells are part of an initiative by the [[Poland|Polish]] Yes to Life foundation. They each weigh more than 2,000 pounds, are nearly four feet in diameter, and were cast by the Felczyński bell foundry in [[Przemyśl]], Poland. [https://www.catholicnewsagency.com/news/249411/pope-francis-blesses-pro-life-bells-going-to-ukraine-and-ecuador (Catholic News Agency)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]], [[Economy of Brazil]]
***The [[Central Bank of Brazil]] raises its [[interest rate]] by 150 [[basis point]]s to 7.75 percent, its largest increase since 2002. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/business-and-tech/20211027-brazil-hikes-interest-rate-by-most-in-two-decades (AFP via RFI)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] begins to vaccinate children in [[Ho Chi Minh City]] where 1,500 teenagers between the ages of 16 and 17 years old are eligible to receive the vaccine as part of an effort to reopen schools after a six-month closure. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-business-health-education-vietnam-9ea049244acb1b062b6ce0df62ef4cc2 (AP)]
****[[Vietnam]] surpasses 900,000 cases of [[COVID-19]]. [https://english.thesaigontimes.vn/vietnams-covid-case-count-surpasses-900000/ (''The Saigon Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] reports a record 5,324 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 184,419. [https://www.todayonline.com/singapore/unusually-high-5324-new-covid-19-cases-spore-10-more-deaths-bring-tally-349 (''Today'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria]]
****[[Bulgaria]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 6,816 new cases of [[COVID-19]], thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 582,122. [http://www.bta.bg/en/c/DF/id/2504587 (Bulgarian News Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 1,123 deaths from COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 233,898. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/russia-marks-daily-coronavirus-death-high-80809704 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] leader [[Keir Starmer]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2021/oct/27/keir-starmer-tests-positive-for-covid (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia]]
***The [[Therapeutic Goods Administration]] approves the usage of the [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] as a [[booster dose]] for people over the age of 18 years old, which can be administered at least six months after the second dose. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-10-27/tga-approves-covid-vaccine-booster-shots-for-over-18-year-olds/100571442 (ABC News Australia)]
**[[COVID-19 drug development]]
***[[Merck & Co.]] signs a licensing agreement with the [[United Nations|UN]]-backed [[Medicines Patent Pool]] that will allow more companies to manufacture generic versions of its experimental oral antiviral COVID-19 treatment [[molnupiravir]] with a royalty-free license that will apply to 105 low- and middle-income countries. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-merck-co/merck-signs-pact-to-broaden-generic-manufacturing-of-covid-19-pill-idUSKBN2HH179 (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Lebanon–Saudi Arabia relations]]
**[[Saudi Arabia]] summons the Lebanese ambassador over "offensive" remarks about the [[Yemeni Civil War (2014-present)|war]] in [[Yemen]] made by Lebanese [[Ministry of Information (Lebanon)|information minister]] [[George Kurdahi]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1956511/saudi-arabia (Arab News)]
*[[China–Tajikistan relations]]
**[[Tajikistan]] approves the construction of a new [[United States dollar|US$]]10 million [[China|Chinese]] military base near [[Afghanistan–Tajikistan border|its border]] with [[Afghanistan]], and in a separate statement offers to hand over a pre-existing base to China and waive future rent payments on the base in exchange for military aid. The approval comes as the Tajik government expressed concerns about the worsening security situation along the border after the [[Taliban]] took over Afghanistan a few months prior. [https://www.rferl.org/a/tajikistan-approves-chinese-base/31532078.html (RFE/RL)]
*[[Nuclear program of Iran]]
**Following a meeting with European officials in [[Brussels]], [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Iranian foreign minister]] [[Hossein Amir-Abdollahian]] announces that negotiations on the [[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action]] will resume in November. Negotiations were halted following the [[United States withdrawal from the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action|United States' withdrawal from the deal]]. [https://www.wionews.com/world/iran-agrees-to-restart-negotiations-on-2015-nuclear-deal-by-november-end-424625 (AFP via WION)] 

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Climate justice]]
**Men from the [[Kalaw Lagaw Ya]] [[Indigenous Australians|Indigenous Australian]] community sue the [[Australian Government]] in the [[Federal Court of Australia|Federal Court]] over the impacts of [[climate change]] on the [[Torres Strait Islands]]. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-10-27/australian-government-sued-for-failing-to-take-climate-action/100569558 (ABC News Australia)]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]], [[Presidency of Jair Bolsonaro]]
**The [[Brazilian Senate]] votes to charge [[President of Brazil|President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] over his controversial handling of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. The [[criminal charge|charges]] include [[crimes against humanity]], incitement to crime, falsification of documents and the violation of social rights. [[Brazil]]'s [[Statistics of the COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil|COVID-19 death toll]] is second only to that of the [[United States]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-59051105 (BBC News)]
*Protests continue for a second consecutive day across [[Ecuador]] due to an increase in the price of [[gasoline]], as president [[Guillermo Lasso]] orders the deployment of security forces to highways in order to maintain order. Lasso also calls on indigenous populations and civil society groups to engage in dialogue. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/ecuador-president-calls-dialogue-with-indigenous-second-day-protests-2021-10-27/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Next Portuguese legislative election]]
**The budget proposed by the [[XXII Constitutional Government of Portugal|Socialist minority government]] of [[Prime Minister of Portugal|Prime Minister]] [[António Costa]] is rejected by the [[Assembly of the Republic (Portugal)|Assembly of the Republic]] for the first time in [[Third Portuguese Republic|the country's democratic history]], following moves by the [[Left Bloc (Portugal)|Left Bloc]] and the [[Portuguese Communist Party|Communist Party]] to join the [[Right-wing politics|right-wing]] parties and reject the budget. It is expected that the [[President of Portugal|President]] [[Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa]] will dissolve the parliament and call for early elections. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20211027-early-polls-likely-as-portugal-mps-reject-budget (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Poland and the European Union]]
**The [[European Court of Justice]] (ECJ) fines [[Poland]] [[Euro|€]]1 million per day, for breaking the law by maintaining the disciplinary chamber of its [[Supreme Court of Poland|Supreme Court]]. The ECJ says Poland has failed to comply with its order, and finds it might pose a "serious and irreparable harm to the legal order of the European Union". The fine is the highest daily penalty the ECJ has ever imposed on any EU member state. [https://www.dw.com/en/eu-fines-poland-1-million-per-day-over-judicial-reforms/a-59635269 (DW)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Homosexuality in association football]]
**[[Australians|Australian]] professional [[Association football|soccer]] player [[Josh Cavallo]] [[comes out]] as [[gay]], becoming the only current openly gay top-flight male soccer player. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/10/27/football/footballer-josh-cavallo-announces-he-is-gay-spt-intl/index.html (CNN)]
